action: No action stated for the public; the agency says it reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission and is investigating with police and outside specialists.
date_note: Date of the Digital Agency announcement as reported by ITmedia; access is said to span 30 July to 12 November and the agency detected it on 12 November.
exec: A Japanese government shared-services file-sharing platform may have leaked files, possibly with personal information, to unintended third parties.
plain: Japan's Digital Agency says people other than the intended recipients accessed files on a government file-sharing service, which may have leaked. It stopped the service on 12 November.

key_findings: The Digital Agency announced on 20 November that some files on the file-sharing service of the government-wide GSS may have leaked.
It detected on 12 November access by people other than the intended recipients and stopped the service that day; access is confirmed so far between 30 July and 12 November.
Files may contain personal information; no secondary harm confirmed so far; reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission.

sources.name: ITmedia: Digital Agency, possible leak at government file-sharing service

summary: ITmedia reports that Japan's Digital Agency announced on 20 November that some files on the file-sharing service of its Government Solutions Service (GSS) may have leaked to outsiders. The agency detected access by people other than intended recipients on 12 November and stopped the service that day; access is confirmed between 30 July and 12 November. The files may contain personal information, no secondary harm is confirmed, and the agency is investigating with police and outside specialists.
title: Japan's Digital Agency says government file-sharing service may have leaked files, third-party access since 30 July

validation.note: Single publisher (ITmedia) relaying the agency's announcement; the agency's own release was not read.
